subject: Re-rank/Emb eval follow-up: retrieval latency & recall@k next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Morgan <alex@searchly.ai>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Apr 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re-rank/Emb eval follow-up: retrieval latency & recall@k next steps

Alex — great to meet today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we can move the competitive eval forward. Thanks again to Priya for joining.

Call recap (high-level):
- Searchly's goal: improve result relevance for product search with reranking layer; current infra calls external embeddings + BM25.
- Primary success metrics you care about: recall@5 / recall@10 lift, P95 retrieval latency, and cost per query at scale.
- Baseline: you'll run current production embedding dims (256) + BM25 baseline. You want to compare Redwood inference + re-ranker vs your hyperscaler baseline.

Redwood proposal / next tests:
1) Retrieval latency: measure end-to-end retrieval P50/P95 (embedding encode + kNN lookup + rerank) for vector dims [128,256,768].
2) Recall tests: recall@1/5/10 on your 50k query holdout. Please mark PASS/FAIL thresholds — we suggest targets: +5-7% recall@5 vs current baseline.
3) Cost profile: estimate per-query token/embed compute cost and storage (vector dims impact) at 100k qps-month scale.
4) Index/config variants: ANN index type (HNSW), vector quantization (8-bit) vs float32 — measure recall vs index size tradeoff.
5) Failover behavior: throughput degradation profile vs our Dedicated/reserved vs hosted fallback.

What we need from you to start the run:
- A 1k sample of queries + 50k doc corpus (anonymized) or a synthetic dataset with similar distributions.
- Preferred vector dims to test first (we recommend 256 -> 128 -> 768).
- Slack access or a shared Drive folder for results.

Attachments: I attached a short eval plan and a small sample script for running batch queries (rerank_eval_plan.pdf, sample_eval_script.py).

Proposed timeline:
- You share data by EOD Thu 04/16
- SE (Aditya) to run initial run and share a results deck by Tue 04/21

Next steps / asks:
- Alex: confirm you can share the dataset and whether 256 is the primary dim to start with.
- Aditya: can you confirm the test infra and estimate how long the first run will take?

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick 30-min sync if useful.

Marissa

Thanks Marissa — this looks good. Quick answers:
- We can share an anonymized 50k doc corpus + 2k query eval set by tomorrow EOD (will drop to the Drive link).
- 256 dims is our current production, so happy to start there and experiment with 128/768 if you recommend.
- For cost calc, include both hosted (per-token/per-embed) and Dedicated reserved pricing estimates — we're evaluating both options.

Two questions from our side:
1) For recall@k comparisons, should we run exact-knn (brute force) as an upper bound?
2) On the vector quantization tests, what quality delta do you typically see for HNSW+8-bit vs float32 for 256-dim on datasets like ours?

We'll upload the dataset to the Drive folder and share access to Priya & me. Also looping in our procurement/infra contact if needed later.

Alex

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.ai>

Date: Thu, 16 Apr 2026 13:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Re-rank/Emb eval follow-up: retrieval latency & recall@k next steps

Alex — great, thanks. A few technical clarifications so we run the right experiments:

- Exact k-NN: yes please include an exact brute-force run (or small-sample brute) as an oracle for recall numbers; we will report recall@1/5/10 relative to that as well as vs your current BM25 baseline.
- Q1: expected quality delta for HNSW + 8-bit vs float32 (256-d): on typical product-search corpora we see ~0.5-1.5% absolute drop in recall@5 for aggressive PQ/8-bit configs; with tuned HNSW params (efConstruction/efSearch) the drop is often <1%. But this varies with distribution — we'll measure.
- Latency measurement: we'll report encoder encode time (P50/P95), ANN lookup P50/P95, reranker scoring P50/P95, and total end-to-end P50/P95. Please indicate whether you measure client-to-endpoint network latencies in your baseline so we can align (we can present both pure server-side and end-to-end numbers).
- Vector dims: we recommend starting at 256 (your prod), then run 128 and 768 for representational/compute tradeoffs. We'll include per-query token/compute cost (rough $/kqps-month) for both hosted and Dedicated.

I've attached the eval plan and a small script to standardize queries. For the run:
- I'll spin up a Dedicated-style instance profile for baseline throughput testing (approx config: 4xA100, batcher tuned for 128-token queries).
- Estimated time for first pass (256 dims, HNSW float32 + rerank): ~6 hours once data is in place; we'll post results in Drive and a short summary deck.

If Alex/Priya can drop the dataset and confirm whether you want brute-force oracle on full 50k or a representative 5k subset, we'll start.

Aditya
